cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hey champ, welcome back! Today's a special one.

cues.caption: Last time: a quarter turn = 90°
cues.text: Last time, you learned about turns. A quarter turn is ninety degrees, and four quarter turns bring you all the way around.

cues.caption: Unit 3 · Chapter 5 · the last one!
cues.text: Today is chapter five, the very last chapter of Unit three, Shapes, Grids and Coordinates.

cues.caption: Chapter 5 · Draw With Math
cues.text: It's called, Draw With Math. We're going to draw shapes using only words and numbers.

cues.caption: Draw with commands, like a programmer!
cues.text: No pencil in your hand. Just clear commands, like a real programmer. Ready? Let's go!

cues.caption: Meet Kachhu, the robot turtle
cues.text: Meet Kachhu. Kachhu is a little robot turtle, with a pen tucked under his tummy. When he walks, he draws a line.

cues.caption: "Kachhu, draw a square!"
cues.text: Your friend Meera puts him on a big sheet of paper, and says, Kachhu, draw a square!

cues.caption: Kachhu doesn't move…
cues.text: And Kachhu just sits there. He doesn't move one bit.

cues.caption: Why didn't Kachhu draw? Think!
cues.text: Hmm. Why not? Think about it for a moment.

cues.caption: He only understands tiny commands
cues.text: Here's the thing. Kachhu doesn't know what a square is. He only understands a few tiny commands. So we have to tell him, step by step, exactly what to do.

cues.caption: Command = one clear instruction
cues.text: A command is one clear instruction. Kachhu knows just two of them.

cues.caption: forward 4 → walk 4 steps, draw a line
cues.text: The first one is, forward. Forward four means, walk four steps straight ahead. His pen is down, so he draws a line as he walks.

cues.caption: The number = how many steps
cues.text: The number tells him how far to go. Forward two makes a short line. Forward eight makes a long one.

cues.caption: turn right 90 → spin a quarter turn
cues.text: The second command is, turn right ninety. Remember last chapter? That's a quarter turn, clockwise. Kachhu spins on the spot. He doesn't walk, so no line is drawn.

cues.caption: Forward draws. Turning spins.
cues.text: So here's the rule. Forward draws. Turning just spins.

cues.caption: A square: 4 equal sides, 4 square corners
cues.text: Now, let's draw that square! First, what does a square have? Four equal sides, and four square corners.

cues.caption: forward 4, turn right 90 · side 1
cues.text: So we say, forward four. Kachhu draws the first side. Then, turn right ninety, for the corner.

cues.caption: Again… side 2. Again… side 3
cues.text: Again! Forward four, turn right ninety. That's side two. And again. Forward four, turn right ninety. Side three.

cues.caption: Side 4 · back to the start!
cues.text: One last time. Forward four, turn right ninety. Look! The lines meet, and Kachhu is back where he started, facing the same way.

cues.caption: 4 times: forward 4, turn right 90
cues.text: Four sides, four corners. A perfect square! We did forward four, turn right ninety, four times.

cues.caption: 8 lines… that's a lot!
cues.text: But writing all eight lines is a lot of work. Phew!

cues.caption: repeat 4 [forward 4, turn right 90]
cues.text: So programmers use a shortcut, called repeat. Repeat four, forward four, turn right ninety. It means, do these two commands, four times.

cues.caption: Repeat = a loop
cues.text: In coding, this is called a loop. Do it, and again, and again.

cues.caption: Commands in order = a tiny program!
cues.text: And a list of commands that a computer follows in order? That's a program. So you just wrote a tiny program! How cool is that?

cues.caption: Bigger square? Which number changes?
cues.text: Now Meera wants a bigger square. Which number should we change? Have a think.

cues.caption: forward 4 → forward 8
cues.text: Just the forward number! Change forward four, into forward eight. Every side gets twice as long.

cues.caption: Keep turn right 90 and repeat 4
cues.text: But keep turn right ninety, and keep repeat four. A square always needs four square corners. Turn only forty-five, and you won't get a square at all!

cues.caption: 4 sides × 4 steps = 16 steps
cues.text: Let's count how far Kachhu walks. Four sides, with four steps each. Four times four, equals sixteen steps.

cues.caption: 4 sides × 8 steps = 32 steps
cues.text: And the big square? Four sides of eight steps. That's thirty-two steps!

cues.caption: Rectangle: long side 6, short side 3
cues.text: What about a rectangle? It has two long sides, and two short sides. Let's make it six steps long, and three steps tall.

cues.caption: forward 6, turn, forward 3, turn
cues.text: Forward six, turn right ninety. Forward three, turn right ninety. That's half of it.

cues.caption: repeat 2 [forward 6, turn, forward 3, turn]
cues.text: Do that two times, and it's done! Repeat two. Forward six, turn right ninety, forward three, turn right ninety.

cues.caption: How many steps in total?
cues.text: So how many steps does Kachhu walk this time? Try adding it up.

cues.caption: 6 + 3 + 6 + 3 = 18 steps
cues.text: Six, plus three, plus six, plus three. That's eighteen steps!

cues.caption: Plus sign · new command: back
cues.text: Here's a fun one. A plus sign! Kachhu starts in the middle, and learns one new command. Back, which means walk backwards.

cues.caption: forward 2, back 2, turn right 90
cues.text: Forward two, back two, turn right ninety. That draws one arm, and brings him back to the middle.

cues.caption: repeat 4 → 4 arms → a plus sign!
cues.text: Repeat that four times, and you get four arms. A plus sign!

cues.caption: Uh-oh! A broken square
cues.text: Uh oh. Meera wrote a square program, but Kachhu drew something strange.

cues.caption: Only 3 sides. How do you fix it?
cues.text: Forward four, turn right ninety. Three times. Only three sides! What's the bug? How would you fix it?

cues.caption: Fix: add one more forward 4
cues.text: Add one more forward four! That draws the missing side. Checking each command in order to find the mistake? That's debugging.

cues.caption: Faces north · forward 2, right 90 · twice
cues.text: One more puzzle. Kachhu faces north, towards the top. He does forward two, turn right ninety, two times. Which way is he facing now?

cues.caption: North → East → South
cues.text: South! The first turn takes him from north to east. The second, from east to south. Two quarter turns make a half turn.

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, your turn to be the programmer! Here's a practice check, just like the quiz.

cues.caption: Write commands: a square, 4 steps a side
cues.text: Write the commands to draw a square, with four steps on each side. Pause the video, and try it on paper.

cues.caption: repeat 4 [forward 4, turn right 90]
cues.text: Here's one way. Forward four, turn right ninety, and do it four times. Or the short way. Repeat four, forward four, turn right ninety. Brilliant!

cues.caption: Square = repeat 4 [forward, turn right 90]
cues.text: Let's remember. A square is, repeat four, forward, then turn right ninety.

cues.caption: Forward number = the size
cues.text: Change the forward number, to change the size.

cues.caption: Forward draws. Turning spins.
cues.text: Forward draws. Turning just spins on the spot.

cues.caption: Commands in order = a tiny program
cues.text: And commands in order make a tiny program.

cues.caption: Chapter 5 done · Unit 3 complete!
cues.text: Chapter five, done! And that means all of Unit three is complete! Shapes, grids, symmetry, turns, and now drawing with commands. Wow, champ!

cues.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
